metadata.title: Zephyr Protocol Security Audit Checklist - Batch 7
metadata.description: Partial checklist covering teleport rejection edges, bridge edges, emergency recovery edges, and subsystem properties (Nova, Withdrawal, Incentive, Hub Aggregation, LayerZero, Stealth, Poseidon, BJJ, IC, Stargate)

checklist.title: Teleport Rejection on Invalid Root Reference

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-TELEPORT-REJECTED-INVALID-ROOT correctly rejects unknown root references.
steps: Locate root validation logic in Verifier withdrawLocal/withdrawGlobal functions
Verify root lookup in provedTransferRoots or globalTransferRoots mapping
Check that non-existent root lookup causes revert with appropriate error
Verify no fallback path bypasses root existence check
Test with fabricated root values that don't exist in storage

executable_checks.description: Submit teleport with non-existent root
executable_checks.focus: Must revert with InvalidRoot or similar error

executable_checks.description: Generate random root values and attempt teleport
executable_checks.focus: All unknown roots must be rejected

checklist.notes: First rejection path in teleport validation chain. Deterministic mapping lookup ensures consistent behavior.

checklist.title: Teleport Rejection on Recipient Hash Mismatch

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-TELEPORT-REJECTED-BAD-RECIPIENT rejects recipient hash mismatches to prevent front-running.
steps: Locate recipient hash validation in Verifier teleport logic
Verify hash is computed from msg.sender (not user parameter)
Check hash comparison with proof public input is strict equality
Verify mismatch triggers revert with appropriate error
Test front-running scenario where attacker submits victim's proof

executable_checks.focus: Hash binding to msg.sender, not caller-controlled value

executable_checks.description: Submit valid proof from different address than proof's recipient
Simulate front-running attack with mempool observation

checklist.notes: Critical anti-front-running protection. Hash collision resistance provides cryptographic guarantee.

checklist.title: Teleport Rejection on Double-Spend Attempt

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-TELEPORT-REJECTED-DOUBLE-SPEND blocks replay attempts via monotonicity check.
steps: Locate totalTeleported tracking and comparison logic
Verify strict inequality check (newTotal > storedTotal, not >=)
Check that replayed proof has equal totalTeleported, triggering rejection
Verify comparison happens before any minting operation
Test replay of previously successful teleport proof

executable_checks.description: Submit same valid proof twice
executable_checks.focus: Second submission must revert with DoubleSpend or similar

executable_checks.description: totalTeleported must be monotonically increasing

checklist.notes: CRITICAL double-spend prevention. Strict inequality guarantees replay rejection.

checklist.title: Teleport Rejection on Invalid Cryptographic Proof

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-TELEPORT-REJECTED-INVALID-PROOF rejects cryptographically invalid proofs via Groth16 verification.
steps: Locate proof verification call to withdrawal decider
Verify Groth16 pairing check is correctly implemented
Check that verification failure causes immediate revert
Verify no execution path bypasses cryptographic verification
Test with malformed proof elements (modified points, scalars)

executable_checks.focus: Proof verification as gate before minting

executable_checks.description: Submit proof with modified elements
Submit proof with wrong public inputs

checklist.notes: Cryptographic rejection path. Groth16 soundness provides overwhelming probability of catching invalid proofs.

checklist.title: Adaptor Unwraps zERC20 Before Bridge

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-ADAPTOR-UNWRAPS ensures zERC20 is burned via LiquidityManager.unwrap() before Stargate bridge.
steps: Locate Adaptor's unwrapAndBridge function
Verify LiquidityManager.unwrap() is called before Stargate.send()
Check that unwrap burns the zERC20 tokens
Verify underlying tokens are received before bridge call
Test that bridge cannot proceed without successful unwrap

executable_checks.description: Verify zERC20 balance decreases before Stargate call
executable_checks.focus: Order of operations: burn then bridge
Verify unwrap is on path to bridge

checklist.notes: Prerequisite ordering ensures atomicity - no path to bridge without burning zERC20.

checklist.title: Bridge Initiated Event Emission

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-BRIDGE-INITIATED emits UnwrapAndBridge event atomically with successful Stargate.send().
steps: Locate event emission in Adaptor's bridge function
Verify UnwrapAndBridge event is emitted after Stargate.send() success
Check event parameters include user, amount, destination chain
Verify no execution path completes bridge without event
Test via transaction log verification

executable_checks.description: Verify event emission in successful bridge transaction

checklist.notes: Success path completion event. Atomic with Stargate.send() success.

checklist.title: Bridge Failure Handling and Fund Recovery

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-BRIDGE-FAILED handles Stargate failure appropriately without leaving user without funds.
steps: Locate error handling for Stargate.send() failures in Adaptor
Verify if unwrap already occurred, refund mechanism exists
Check that underlying tokens are not stuck in Adaptor
Verify user receives either underlying or zERC20 back
Test Stargate failure scenarios (reverts, insufficient liquidity)

executable_checks.description: Simulate Stargate.send() failure after unwrap
executable_checks.focus: User must be able to recover underlying tokens

executable_checks.description: Test with mock Stargate that always fails

checklist.notes: Potential fund risk if unwrap succeeds but bridge fails. Implementation must ensure recovery path.

checklist.title: Emergency Recovery State Transition

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-EMERGENCY-RECOVERED correctly transitions to recovered state under owner control.
steps: Locate deactivateEmergency or equivalent function
Verify owner-only access control
Check that emergency flag is cleared
Verify transition only possible from emergency state
Test recovery can only be performed by owner

executable_checks.description: Attempt recovery from non-owner account
Recovery from owner during emergency state

checklist.notes: Admin-controlled recovery. Accepted trust assumption that owner makes sound judgment.

checklist.title: Return to Idle State After Recovery

detection_procedure.description: Verify that EDGE-BACK-TO-IDLE correctly returns Verifier to normal operation after recovery.
steps: Locate the state transition logic after emergency deactivation
Verify normal protocol functions are re-enabled
Check that idle state allows standard operations (prove, teleport)
Verify no residual emergency state affects behavior
Test normal operations work after recovery

executable_checks.focus: Emergency flag cleared enables normal functions

executable_checks.description: After recovery, attempt standard prove operation
Full cycle: normal -> emergency -> recovered -> normal
executable_checks.focus: State machine completes full cycle correctly

checklist.notes: Final recovery step. Transition only from STATE-EMERGENCY-RECOVERED.

checklist.title: Nova IVC Proof Generation Soundness

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-NOVA-PROOF-GENERATION produces valid Nova IVC proofs from historical transfer data without leaking private information.
steps: Review Nova proof generation code in CLI client
Verify correct R1CS circuit instantiation for transfer history
Check witness assignment includes only authorized user data
Verify local IVC verification before submission
Test proof generation with known test vectors

executable_checks.description: Generate proof and verify locally
Verify proof doesn't contain witness data

checklist.notes: Client-side proof generation. Nova soundness guarantees invalid witness fails.

checklist.title: Nova to Groth16 Conversion Correctness

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-NOVA-TO-GROTH16 correctly converts IVC proofs to Groth16 format for on-chain verification.
steps: Locate Decider/Prover service conversion code
Verify same circuit is used for both Nova and Groth16
Check public input extraction matches circuit expectations
Verify Groth16 proving key is correctly configured
Test conversion with known valid IVC proofs

executable_checks.description: Generate IVC, convert to Groth16, verify on-chain

checklist.notes: Mathematical equivalence ensures proof correspondence between formats.

checklist.title: On-Chain Nova Proof Verification

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-NOVA-PROOF-VERIFICATION performs complete on-chain verification of transfer root proofs.
steps: Locate proveTransferRoot function in Verifier
Verify IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof is called
Check reserved checkpoint is used as public input
Verify storage only occurs after successful verification
Test with invalid proofs to confirm rejection

executable_checks.description: Submit invalid Nova proof

checklist.notes: Groth16 zkSNARK verification. Invalid proofs fail pairing check.

checklist.title: Withdrawal Proof Verification Completeness

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-WITHDRAWAL-PROOF-VERIFICATION verifies withdrawal proofs for all teleport operations.
steps: Locate withdrawLocal and withdrawGlobal functions
Verify proof type detection (Nova vs Groth16)
Check correct decider selection based on proof type
Verify public input extraction is consistent
Test both local and global withdrawal paths

executable_checks.description: Test local withdrawal with valid proof
Test global withdrawal with valid proof

checklist.notes: Both Nova and Groth16 paths perform cryptographic verification.

checklist.title: Incentive Curve Calculation Correctness

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-INCENTIVE-CURVE correctly computes incentives using linear density integration with proper rounding.
steps: Locate IncentiveLib in LiquidityManager
Verify density calculation formula matches specification
Check floor rounding for rewards, ceiling for fees
Verify target clamping prevents over-incentivization
Test edge cases (zero liquidity, at target, max liquidity)

executable_checks.description: Test incentive calculation at various liquidity levels
Fuzz liquidity amounts and verify invariants

checklist.notes: Deterministic formula. Rounding direction protects protocol from manipulation.

checklist.title: Hub Aggregation Tree Computation

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-HUB-AGGREGATION computes correct PoseidonT3 aggregation tree from token roots.
steps: Locate aggregation logic in Hub contract
Verify PoseidonT3 hash function is used
Check tree construction follows correct ordering
Verify circom compatibility for circuit matching
Test aggregation with known roots and expected output

executable_checks.focus: Correct tree construction and hash usage

executable_checks.description: Compute aggregation with test vectors
Verify aggregated root is usable in withdrawal proofs

checklist.notes: PoseidonT3 is deterministic. Circom-compatible configuration ensures circuit compatibility.

checklist.title: LayerZero Message Flow with EID Validation

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-LAYERZERO-MESSAGE-FLOW delivers cross-chain messages with proper EID validation on receive.
steps: Locate all _lzReceive implementations (Hub, Verifier)
Verify EID validation is first check in each handler
Check that unknown EIDs cause message rejection
Verify peer registry is correctly maintained
Test message reception from unauthorized source

executable_checks.description: Send message from unregistered EID
Send message from registered peer

checklist.notes: EID validation on receiver rejects unknown sources. Guardian supermajority provides integrity.

checklist.title: Stealth Address Generation Unlinkability

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-STEALTH-ADDRESS-GENERATION produces unlinkable stealth addresses with PoW protection.
steps: Locate stealth address generation code in CLI
Verify keccak256-based derivation is used
Check Baby JubJub scalar multiplication is correct
Verify PoW nonce search prevents enumeration
Test that generated addresses cannot be linked to sender

executable_checks.description: Generate multiple stealth addresses from same sender
Check address distribution for patterns

checklist.notes: keccak256 preimage resistance and BJJ discrete log hardness provide cryptographic guarantee.

checklist.title: Poseidon Hash Circuit Compatibility

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-POSEIDON-HASH-CIRCUIT computes circom-compatible Poseidon hashes.
steps: Locate Poseidon implementation in Solidity and Rust
Verify configuration matches circom light-poseidon
Check round constants and MDS matrix are identical
Compare output with circom reference implementation
Test with known test vectors

executable_checks.description: Compare hash output with circom reference
Use on-chain hash in ZK circuit

checklist.notes: Same parameters as circom produce identical output. Critical for ZK circuit compatibility.

checklist.title: Baby JubJub Curve Operations Correctness

detection_procedure.description: Verify that GRAPH-BABY-JUBJUB-OPERATIONS performs correct elliptic curve operations on Baby JubJub.
steps: Locate BJJ implementation in SDK/CLI
Verify curve parameters match specification
Check point addition and scalar multiplication
Verify point validation rejects invalid points
Test with known test vectors for curve operations

executable_checks.description: Test curve operations with known vectors
Attempt operations with invalid points

checklist.notes: Deterministic curve arithmetic. ECDLP hardness protects private scalars.
